pinnedSource.src/endpoints/stable-diffusion.js:1473: bfl: POST https://api.bfl.ai/v1/<model> with a fixed projection, then up to 100 polls of the provider polling_url or https://api.bfl.ai/v1/get_result?id=<id> after delay(2500), each poll carrying x-key, then a bare fetch of result.sample
pinnedSource.src/endpoints/stable-diffusion.js:1641: falai: POST queue.fal.run/fal-ai/<model>, then up to 100 status polls after delay(2500), then the response_url from the STATUS answer, then images[0].url, all with "Key <key>" auth; the catch answers error.cause || error.message

mechanism: Every upstream is a hardcoded literal, so the probe replaces the `node-fetch` module and the global `fetch` with a controlled peer (tools/lib/pinned-outbound.mjs); the Go side uses its own seams for the two provider bases and replays the recorded rules through a real local listener, rewriting the provider-supplied follow-up URLs onto it.

fields.reason: Express and the pinned middleware stack set them; a string body is html-typed and an object cause is json-typed
the projection, including the base64 image payload and the fal.ai cause text/JSON
the first hop is the seam plus the RAW model interpolation; the follow-up hops are the URLs the provider handed back, compared as path+query because the host is the provider's choice
JSON member order and the omitted-undefined members of the projection; seeds are NOT masked because both routes forward the caller seed
the declared provider headers, asserted in BOTH directions by the test (x-key versus Authorization, and the key carried to the image host)
the poll COUNT is fixture data, produced by `times`-bounded rules; the replay refuses a different count

a two-way bucket (under 2s / at least one 2500ms delay). A duration would be host-derived; the bucket only proves the loop waited. The Go replay collapses the interval through a test seam, so this is evidence about the PINNED run; separate Go tests pin the interval and the attempt count.
the timed rule list the peer served, so a scenario can be re-driven from the fixture alone
the secrets file the probe wrote, so a reader can see which key each branch used

normalizations: Synthetic credentials and synthetic image bytes only.
The provider-supplied follow-up hosts are synthetic (bfl-poll/bfl-media/fal-status/fal-result/fal-media.example.test), so no recording can be mistaken for live provider data.
The seed is recorded EXACTLY, not masked: these two routes forward the caller seed, so masking it would let an implementation that defaulted it pass.

notCovered.bfl timeout: The 100-attempt exhaustion branch needs 100 polls of delay(2500), about four minutes of wall clock, so it is NOT recorded; shortening the delay in the probe would record a behaviour the product does not have. It is covered by a LABELLED Go implementation test (TestSDBFLTimeoutIsAnImplementationTest), and the pinned observable is that the handler answers NOTHING after the loop runs out.
notCovered.falai timeout: Same branch on the same reasoning; see TestSDFalaiTimeoutIsAnImplementationTest.
notCovered.reserved-character job id in the bfl fal: The fallback template interpolates the task id into a QUERY (`?id=<id>`). A recorded id containing a space would be re-encoded by the pinned URL parser and re-sent verbatim by the Go transport, which is an unresolved divergence rather than a covered behaviour, so only a plain token id is recorded. Real BFL task ids are opaque tokens.
notCovered.falai non-JSON result document: The pinned catch would answer the JS SyntaxError message, which is a V8 version string rather than a product decision, so no scenario records it; the Go side answers a plain 500 there and the difference is a KNOWN, UNPINNED gap.
notCovered.bfl Ready status without result.sample: The pinned code fetches `undefined`, which node-fetch rejects, so the pinned server answers 500. It is NOT recordable through the controlled peer: the peer records the request for the string "undefined", finds no rule and synthesises a 500 RESPONSE, and because the sample fetch has no ok check the route turns that synthesised answer into a 200 image of the stub text. Recording it would be a probe artefact presented as an oracle, so the branch is covered by the LABELLED Go implementation test TestSDBFLMissingSampleIsAnImplementationTest instead.
